llm.summary: This appears to be a legitimate deep-research helper, but it needs Review because it can fetch arbitrary URLs and send research data and API keys to configurable LLM endpoints without strong destination controls.

dimensions.detail: Environment variables are used for LLM and GitHub credentials, which fits the purpose, but custom LLM base URLs are accepted without scheme or host validation while bearer credentials and research prompts are sent to them.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, dependency bootstrap, startup hook, scheduled task, or tool hijacking behavior was found in the inspected artifacts; usage is via documented Python scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses web search, web fetch, provider configuration, sub-agent orchestration, checkpoints, and output files, but it does not clearly scope allowed network destinations or warn prominently that fetched content and user questions may be sent to third-party LLM providers.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill documents and implements user-directed local output, checkpoints, and research-memory files. This is purpose-aligned, but those files can retain sensitive questions, sources, intermediate findings, and reports.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is coherent: multi-stage web, GitHub, docs, LLM scoring, reflection, and report writing. The concern is that the implemented URL fetchers accept arbitrary HTTP(S) destinations, which goes beyond ordinary public research retrieval and can reach internal or attacker-controlled endpoints.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with the skill making outbound web, GitHub, documentation, and LLM-provider requests. Avoid confidential research topics unless you control the provider endpoint and local workspace, prefer HTTPS trusted endpoints, review any custom LLM base URL carefully, and treat checkpoints/output files as potentially sensitive retained data.
llm.findings:
[TT3] unexpected: Confirmed in llm_client.py: environment-selected base URLs receive bearer API credentials and prompt data through urllib without destination validation. This is not evidence of malicious intent, but it is overbroad for credential-bearing network calls.
[TP4] expected: External LLM/provider use is disclosed in SKILL.md and DOCS.md, so this is not hidden tool poisoning; the remaining issue is incomplete disclosure of data egress boundaries and supported destinations.
[SQP-2] expected: The pipeline is designed to send questions, chunks, findings, and drafts through LLM stages and optionally persist checkpoints. That behavior fits deep research, but privacy and retention warnings are not prominent enough.
[E1] expected: Calls to OpenAI-compatible, Z.AI, DuckDuckGo, GitHub, docs, and example provider URLs are expected for this skill. They are security-relevant external transmissions, not validated evidence of exfiltration.
[LP3] unexpected: The package has no meaningful permission metadata, while the scripts require network access, environment credentials, and local file writes. This is a governance and scoping gap.
[RA2] expected: Research directories, output files, and checkpoints are documented and user-directed. The concern is data retention, not covert persistence.
[EA2] unexpected: The cited phrase is an integrity rule about checking sources, not autonomous destructive or financial action. I do not treat this as a supported high-impact agency finding.
[SSD-4] expected: LLM ranking and synthesis over retrieved content is core to the skill, but source text is mixed into prompts with limited prompt-injection hardening, which can affect report integrity.
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed arbitrary URL fetching in research_sources.py, context_expander.py, and research_pipeline.py. Lack of public-address validation creates a real SSRF-style risk if untrusted URLs enter search results or inputs.
[T01] expected: Confirmed indirect prompt-injection exposure from fetched web content entering LLM scoring, extraction, and writing prompts. This primarily threatens research integrity, not local code execution.
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed custom LLM endpoints can receive Authorization headers and research payloads without HTTPS or private-address enforcement. This warrants Review rather than a malicious verdict because the feature is documented provider configuration.
